explanation.headline: Garage One fell short of orbit because Stage 1 lost too much Δv to gravity, drag and steering
explanation.why: The vehicle delivered only 7 724 m/s total Δv while 7 612.6 m/s orbital speed is needed, but after subtracting losses (Stage 1: 902 m/s gravity, 187 m/s drag, 193 m/s steering; Stage 2: 176 m/s gravity, 4 m/s drag, 49 m/s steering) the effective Δv available for velocity gain is insufficient, leaving perigee at 137 km (<150 km) and apogee at 153.9 km.

vehicle.note: Korea's three-stage launcher.

explanation.headline: Stage 1 gravity loss consumes most of the Δv budget, leaving the vehicle short of the speed needed for a 700 km circular orbit
explanation.why: Stage 1 was required to provide an ideal 3070 m/s but delivered only 1909 m/s – a loss of 893 m/s to gravity, 68 m/s to drag and 202 m/s to steering (≈1.16 km/s total). Stages 2 and 3 also lose smaller amounts (364 m/s gravity, 2 m/s drag, 39 m/s steering and 138 m/s gravity, 0 m/s drag, 132 m/s steering respectively), so the summed delivered Δv of 7959 m/s falls short of the ~9796 m/s ideal needed to reach the 7504 m/s orbital speed. Reducing mass and increasing Stage 1 thrust recover the missing Δv, allowing the vehicle to meet the target perigee/apogee of ~705 km.

Keep at least 30 minutes for command upload. Max 1.0 m/s per burn.
